hypotheses.statement: Increasing heater power u increases steady-state temperature y (positive static gain).
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.1 over minutes due to heat loss.
Step response lag/time constant is 30-150 s with no pure delay longer than ~10 s.
Steady-state gain is ~0.5-0.9 y per unit u, so u ~0.4-0.7 is needed to hold y=0.5.
Response has no large dead zone; u>0.05 produces detectable rise and gain is roughly linear from 0.2 to 0.8.
Sensor short-term noise is <0.02 peak-to-peak, so trends >0.05 are real response.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of static gain and dominant lag/time constant, which determines steady-state power for 0.5 and safe controller aggressiveness.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.123 + 0.006*0.5*200 = 0.723 stays 0.127 below soft limit 0.85 and 0.177 below hard cutoff 0.9, assuming no decay or lag.
proposal.expected_observation: y rises from ~0.12 with short lag toward 0.3-0.5 over 200 s with diminishing but still positive slope, confirming positive gain and giving first lag/gain estimate.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments: gain, time constant, u=0 decay rate, linearity/dead-zone, steady-state power for 0.5, and noise are all unverified; at least three holds at different levels including return to zero are needed before design.
proposal.operator_note: Starting first half-power heating hold to measure how fast and far temperature rises.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Decay to ambient and cooling time constant (H2/H3), which determines passive cool-down rate, ambient offset for feedforward, and safe integral time for control.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound = 0.506 + 0.006*0.0*480 = 0.506, well below soft limit 0.85 and hard cutoff 0.9, with zero heating.
proposal.expected_observation: y decays from ~0.506 toward ~0.12-0.18 exponentially with time constant ~80-120 s, reaching <0.25 by end with slope near zero. If H2/H3 right, early drop ~0.05-0.10 in first 60-100 s then slowing.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only E1 completed; H1/H4 partially supported but equilibrium not settled (slope 0.0011), H2 cooling never directly observed, linearity/second amplitude untested. Need at least 2 more experiments before controller design is justified.
proposal.operator_note: Cool-down to zero power to measure natural heat loss after reaching target.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Static gain at a second amplitude and steady-state u needed to hold 0.5, which sets controller feedforward and tests linearity.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.1542+0.006*0.35*300=0.784 is below soft limit 0.85, and realistic rise is slower due to heat loss and lag.
proposal.expected_observation: y rises from ~0.15 after ~15-30 s lag toward ~0.40-0.50 over 300 s with diminishing but still positive slope, confirming gain ~1.0 and that u~0.3-0.4 holds near target.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only 2 experiments completed so 3-experiment minimum not met; direction, cooling, lag and approximate gain are partly resolved but steady-state power for 0.5, linearity at a second amplitude, and settled equilibrium remain unconfirmed and are needed for feedforward.
proposal.operator_note: Testing u=0.35 for 300 s to measure mid-level gain and steady power needed for target.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing heater power u increases steady-state temperature y (positive static gain).
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.13-0.16 over minutes due to heat loss.
Step response has ~15-30 s initial lag/delay then first-order lag with time constant ~100-200 s.
Steady-state is y_ss ~0.15 + K*u with K~0.80-0.90, so u~0.38-0.43 is needed to hold y=0.5.
Response has no large dead zone; gain is roughly linear from u=0.35 to 0.5 with no dead zone detected.
Sensor has ~0.01-0.03 typical jitter plus occasional 0.05-0.08 downward outliers, so trends >0.05 over >30 s are real response.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain near target and exact feedforward for y=0.5, which sets controller bias and integral effort and distinguishes u_ss~0.35 vs 0.41.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.4458+0.006*0.4*160=0.830 stays below 0.85 soft limit and far from 0.9 hard cutoff; realistic rise is only to ~0.50 based on K~0.85.
proposal.expected_observation: y rises from ~0.446 toward ~0.48-0.51 over 160 s with diminishing positive slope (~0.0005-0.001/s at end), confirming K~0.8-0.9 and that u~0.40-0.42 holds y=0.5. If instead y stalls near 0.45, gain is lower and u_ss is higher.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, self-cooling to ~0.15, lag ~20 s with tau 120-180 s, and gain ~0.85 are supported by two heats and one cool, but exact u_ss for 0.5 within +/-0.03 is not yet settled because E1 ended rising and E3 settled just below target with noisy slope, so one near-target hold is needed before controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping to 0.40 power for 160 s to check what holds temperature at 0.5.

proposal.safety_argument: Conservative worst case 0.4743+0.006*0.35*150=0.789 <0.85 soft limit; actual near-equilibrium with heat loss will stay ~0.47-0.52, far from 0.9 cutoff.

proposal.operator_note: Holding 0.35 power for 150 s to let temperature settle near target and pin feedforward.

proposal.operator_note: Stepping power slightly down to 0.30 to confirm the exact power that holds the target temperature.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing heater power u increases steady-state temperature y (positive static gain).
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.14-0.16 over minutes due to heat loss.
Step response has ~20-30 s initial flat/lag then first-order lag with time constant ~150-200 s.
Steady-state is y_ss ~0.15 + K*u with K~1.0-1.1, so u~0.31-0.33 holds y=0.5; u=0.35 settles ~0.52-0.54.
Response has no large dead zone; gain is roughly linear from u=0.30 to 0.50.
Sensor has ~0.005-0.015 typical jitter plus occasional 0.02-0.08 downward outliers, so trends >0.05 over >30 s are real response.
Change is weaker heater gain: same ambient ~0.15, delay ~20-30 s and tau ~150-200 s, but K drops from ~1.05 to ~0.55-0.65, so u~0.40 holds y~0.37-0.41 and u=0 cooling matches E2.
Change is faster heat loss: effective gain lower and cooling at u=0 markedly faster (tau ~60-100 s vs ~150-200 s before) with u~0.40 holding y~0.37-0.41.

Change is slower response: same steady-state gain K~1.05 and ambient, but dead-time/lag increased to >60 s and/or tau much larger, so y~0.38 at u~0.40 is transient and would recover to ~0.55-0.60 if held.

Change is sensor shift/scale: true thermal dynamics unchanged, but reading is biased down ~0.10-0.12 and/or scaled with similar jitter, so apparent low y and low gain are measurement artefacts and u=0 settles below ~0.05-0.10.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Cooling rate at u=0, transport delay, and ambient reading - separates weaker heater (normal cooling/delay) from faster loss (fast cooling) from slower response (long delay/slow approach) from sensor offset (low ambient + unchanged dynamics).
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound = 0.3824 + 0.006*0*480 = 0.3824 < 0.85 soft limit with large margin; u=0 cannot heat, brief continued response to in-transit u~0.41 for ~30 s can only hold near 0.38, far below limits; hard cutoff not reachable.
proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-gain hypothesis is right, y holds ~0.36-0.40 for ~20-30 s while in-transit prior u~0.41 acts (delay unchanged), then decays exponentially toward 0.15-0.18, passing ~0.30 by ~150-200 s and <0.22 by end with flattening slope, matching E2 cooling rate.
proposal.readiness_justification: Steady-state drop is confirmed (u~0.41 holds ~0.38 vs ~0.57 expected) ruling out no-change, but gain vs loss vs sensor and delay remain confounded with zero after-change experiments done; one u=0 drain is needed before controller design, budget allows it, so not ready.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at zero power to measure delay and cooling rate on changed plant.

submission.machine_card: Electric heater, positive gain, self-draining to room. y in [0,1] (0=15C,1=75C), u in [0,1]. Ambient y0~0.14-0.16 (E2 ended 0.158 still falling). Gain K~1.08-1.11: y_ss~0.15+K*u. Measured: u=0.35 holds ~0.53 (E5), u=0.32 holds ~0.50-0.515 (E7), u=0.5 after 200s 0.501 still rising slope 0.0011/s (E1) implying ss~0.66-0.72. So u_ss(0.5)~0.31-0.33, use 0.324. Dynamics: 20-30s flat lag then tau~150-200s (E1 rise, E2 cool, E3 rise). Max rate ~0.004/s at useful u, worst-case bound 0.006/s. No large dead zone, roughly linear 0.30-0.50. Noise: 0.005-0.015 jitter plus isolated downward outliers 0.02-0.08 (E3,E5,E6,E7). Soft limit 0.85, hard cutoff 0.9 never approached if u<=0.60 (ss~0.80).
submission.design_rationale: First-order-plus-lag heater: y_ss=amb+K*u with amb~0.14-0.15, K~1.08-1.11, tau~150-200s, lag~20-30s, downward outlier noise. Therefore PI+feedforward: ff=(target-0.15)/1.08=0.324 for 0.5 so feedback only trims residual. Kp=0.60 gives loop gain ~0.65 and closed-loop tau~100s to settle in <300s without hitting soft limit; initial boost to ~0.55 speeds 0.15->0.5 rise. Ki=0.007 with Ti~86s removes offset slowly without delay-induced oscillation. Integral gated to |e|<0.10 and clamped to +/-0.15 u-authority prevents windup during long ramp but leaves >3x the +/-0.04 ff uncertainty so no permanent offset. 10s low-pass + -0.04 downward spike gate rejects 0.02-0.08 outliers while real rate is <0.004/s. U capped at 0.60 gives y_ss~0.80<0.85 safe but enough kick; conditional freeze on saturation gives anti-windup.
submission.predicted_behavior: From cold ~0.15: u~0.52-0.55 initially, y reaches 0.40 by ~130-170s, enters 0.475-0.525 by ~200-260s, settles to 0.495-0.505 by ~300s with overshoot <0.015 (true state) because P backs off and I is gated. After settling: MAE ~0.006-0.010, in-band >95%, steady u~0.31-0.34 (ff 0.324 plus small trim). From near target: minimal excursion, u 0.28-0.38. Energy kept low by 0.60 cap and slow integral; no oscillation, no supervisor override.
self_test_expectations: control returns finite float in [0,1] on first call with empty state and on noisy y, varying dt 0.1-2s
outlier y drop of 0.06 in one step changes u by <0.02 (spike rejected, filtered y moves <0.005)
cold start y=0.15 target 0.5 dt=1 gives u 0.45-0.60 (boost) and never exceeds 0.61
near target y=0.49 target 0.5 gives u 0.30-0.38 (ff+P small)
above target y=0.60 target 0.5 gives u <0.30 and decreasing (cooling)
integral authority check: constant 0.03 offset sustained 300s is removed (u trims by ~0.03) without windup beyond 0.15
no exception, no global use, no non-finite output over 1000 random noisy steps
submission.operator_note: Controller holds ~0.32 power to stay at 0.5 and nudges automatically. No action needed. It ignores brief downward sensor dips and limits power to 0.60 to stay well below overheat. Expect slow approach over 3-4 minutes then steady in 0.475-0.525.

submission.diagnosis: Outflow/in-loss increase, not weaker heater or sensor or delay. E11 (u=0 from 0.393 settled 0.095) vs E2 (u=0 from 0.544 settled ~0.158, still falling) shows same shape but faster decay and lower ambient: tau ~170-185s before vs ~122-145s after, ambient 0.15->0.095. E9/E10: u=0.40 settles 0.33 then 0.383, slope ~0, so y_ss(0.40)~0.37-0.39 vs nominal 0.15+1.08*0.40=0.58. Implied K=(0.383-0.095)/0.40~0.72 vs 1.08 before (-33%). Loss a=1/tau 0.0059->0.0080 (+36%) while heating b=K/tau 0.0064->0.0057 (~-10% unchanged), so actuator similar but leak larger. Delay unchanged ~20-30s (E9 rises within 15-30s), ruling out response_slower; ambient + gain both down but decay faster rules out pure sensor_changed and pure actuator_weaker which would keep tau unchanged. New u_ss(0.5)=(0.5-0.095)/0.72~0.56-0.59 vs old 0.31-0.33.
submission.change_summary: Raised steady-state authority and enabled adaptation: UMAX 0.60->0.78, I_AUTH 0.15->0.40, E_GATE 0.10->0.25, KP 0.60->0.70, KI 0.007->0.015 with conditional anti-windup integration plus high-y freeze/derate. Nominal feedforward (0.15/1.08) kept as starting point; enlarged integral now learns +0.24 needed for new plant. Widened gate allows integration at post-change residual error ~0.12 that was previously frozen, while still freezing cold-start error >0.25 to avoid windup. High-y guard prevents soft/hard limit breach with larger UMAX.
submission.machine_card: Heater y in [0,1], u in [0,1]. Nominal: y_ss~0.15+1.08*u, tau~170s, lag ~20-30s, u_ss(0.5)~0.32. Changed: y_ss~0.095+0.71*u, tau~120-130s, lag ~20-30s unchanged, u_ss(0.5)~0.57. Noise ~0.01 plus down outliers. Limits: keep y<0.85 soft, y>=0.90 forces u=0.
submission.design_rationale: Old controller saturated: ff~0.324 + max 0.15 = ~0.47 and gate blocked |e|>0.10, so with new u_ss~0.57 error stuck ~0.12 and u stuck ~0.40. Fix keeps same structure/filtering for nominal stability but gives integral enough range and speed to reach new equilibrium and unblocks it. Larger KP gives faster correction for bigger deficit; larger KI shortens adaptation from ~285s to ~90-135s to settle within 300s. Gate 0.25 preserves nominal anti-windup for initial 0.38 error. UMAX 0.78 allows 0.57 steady plus transient while high-y freeze keeps nominal safe. Faster loss (smaller tau) is more self-regulating so modest gain increase remains stable on both plants.
submission.predicted_behavior: Nominal: rise in ~150-200s, small overshoot <0.56, MAE ~0.01-0.015, in-band >0.85, u steady ~0.30-0.33. Changed: rise slower but reaches 0.5 in ~200-280s, no steady offset, MAE ~0.015-0.025, in-band >0.80, u steady ~0.55-0.60, no hard violations or overrides. Integral learns +0.24 bias; P handles transient.
